draft.headline: Rebalance toward bonds and fix the TFSA placement
draft.summary: Daniel's portfolio is {{m:drift.US_EQUITY.pp}} overweight US equity and {{m:drift.CA_BONDS.pp}} underweight bonds after a strong US rally. His US-listed fund sits in the TFSA, where foreign withholding is a permanent cost, and {{m:tax.tfsa_room.cad}} of room is unused while {{m:tax.nonreg_interest.cad}} of interest-bearing cash sits non-registered. Volatility of {{m:risk.vol.pct}} is inside the balanced band.

actions.description: Trim US equity and add to Canadian bonds to return to the balanced targets.
actions.rationale: Both drifts exceed tolerance; Daniel prefers few trades, so one rebalance now.

actions.description: Hold the US-listed fund in the RRSP instead of the TFSA.
actions.rationale: Treaty exemption applies in an RRSP, not a TFSA.

actions.description: Move the non-registered cash into the TFSA.
actions.rationale: Shelters taxable interest using unused room.

risks_and_considerations: Rebalancing in the non-registered account may realise gains.
client_talking_points: Your mix drifted with the US rally; we bring it back to plan.
A small account change removes a permanent tax cost.
